_doc: NØRDING dating cabinet (#29, Wave D, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #35). Erik Nørding (blacksmith-engineer): started as SON (Skovbo og Nørding) in the early 1960s, renamed NØRDING mid-'60s after the partnership split. Grading letters + the SON precursor window are the levers. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Nording.json (Chuck Stanion interview — detailed) + Dennis Dreyer photo captions ('Early 1960s SON D Grade'). Single-source brackets = approx-flagged.

history_anchors._doc: Erik Nørding: blacksmith at 15, then engineering (father's razor-blade factory). Pipe machinery built for repairman SKOVBO -> unpaid -> partnership: SON pipes (Skovbo Og Nørding acronym), early 1960s; each partner borrowed $5,500. Skovbo quits the partnership ('you'll never be a pipemaker') -> by the legal agreement Nørding KEEPS the company, pays Skovbo off over 5 years. 'Continued with SON pipes for only a year or two before changing the company name to NØRDING in the mid-60s.' Exclusively freehands at first; graded A/B/C/D + EXTRA (highest); an F grade added LATER (cheaper than A). 1970s-early-80s = the freehand boom: peak 52 workers. Later: ~6 makers, ~15k pipes/yr (interview era ~2001); today ~50k/yr with 90% export (intro paragraph — figures vary by era). Handmades (acrylic bits, ~300/month) vs machine-roughed freehands (vulcanite). Hunting Series = annual themed pipe (running by 2001; start year not documented). Giant Guinness-record pipe (Copenhagen airport). Seconds: AALBØRG, ERIKSEN; 'Sorn' also made by Nørding. Briar: Corsica + Greece.

brand_marks.physical: SON-era: 'SON' stamp + grade letter (A-D), some with horn shank extensions; 'SON Pradikat' line existed. Nørding-era: script/block Nørding + grade letter (A-E... F later, EXTRA top); Hunting Series = annual motif; high grades with sterling mounts (Nørding 18, 20).

line_years._notes: Hunting Series: annual, running by 2001 — start year undocumented -> unencoded. NORD-COAT / AS / FS lines pictured, undated. Grade letters span the brand -> never encoded. F grade 'added later' — year unknown.
